newsitem.title: GERMANY: Institutes urge Bonn to act soon on fiscal reforms.
newsitem.headline: Institutes urge Bonn to act soon on fiscal reforms.

text.p: Germany's six leading economic institutes on Tuesday, noting that uncertainty about economic monetary union and fiscal policies were hurting the economy, urged the government to act quickly to carry out fiscal reforms.

The institutes' latest economic report, to be presented at a news conference later on Tuesday, said the government's fiscal policies were marked by efforts to cut the deficit in its drive to qualify for monetary union and dealing with the costs of high unemployment.

"Uncertainty about achieving the Maastricht criteria and doubts about the consistency of fiscal policies have in fact led to misunderstandings that have considerably burdened the economic climate," the institutes said in their report.

The report said it was necessary to establish clarity as soon as possible about the direction of financial policies during the rest of the year, what the planned tax reform will look like, and which measures will be grasped on the spending side in order to secure budget consolidation.
"Getting rid of these uncertainties alone would have positive impact on the investment climate," the report said.
